long_biography.plain_text:
Doukas entered journalism as a shipping reporter at Ethnikos Kirix in 1963 and soon moved into newspaper editorial leadership. He worked across dailies and maritime titles, served for two decades as the Greece correspondent of France's Journal de la Marine Marchande, and founded the shipping magazines ELNAVI and NAFS. Those institutions gave him a lasting place in the country's maritime press.

Alongside journalism, he pursued Homeric and Greek-language research for four decades. He translated the Iliad and Odyssey in prose and verse and compiled dictionaries and studies. He also advanced a theory connecting Homeric Ithaca with Lefkada, where he spent part of each year. The Journalists' Union of Athens Daily Newspapers entrusted him with a seminar series on the history and development of Greek. Doukas died in 2025; his sons Panagiotis and Nikolaos continued the family's NAFS work.
